title: Create with Thorntale AI
summary: Need a slide deck stat and don't have time to make it yourself? Let Thorntale AI do the heavy lifting!
body_text: We’ve all been there: your meeting is in 5 minutes and you’re supposed to present. But your slides aren’t ready! Panic no longer. We’ve upgraded Thorntale AI with a full deck creation engine, allowing you to create a perfect deck from scratch in less time than it takes to make your morning coffee. Thorntale’s deck creation can start from a set of notes, a quick brief, or even one line of text. Thorntale first generates an outline for you to approve, allowing you to make any modifications or add more context before it creates full slides. When you’re ready, select your theme then hit ‘Generate Deck’ to get your slides. We’ve also added AI Quick Actions to make it faster and easier to modify slides after you’ve created your presentation. You can find these under the AI icon in the slide menu. Of course, you can still ask Thorntale AI directly to make any changes we don’t have a quick action for. We’d love to hear about how you use Thorntale AI!

title: Equities update | July 24th, 2026
summary: AI spending reshaped equity markets as Bitcoin miners outperformed, the CLARITY Act advanced, and investors assessed earnings, inflation risks and blockchain equities.
body_text: Home Insights Research & data Equities update | July 24th, 2026 6 min read Week 30 was characterised by continued volatility across major US equity indices as rising AI capital expenditure weighed on mega-cap technology stocks, particularly following Alphabet’s first negative free-cash-flow quarter in several years. Price action remained highly bifurcated: capital-intensive hyperscalers and software companies faced pressure over the timing of returns on AI investment, while data-centre operators, power providers and former Bitcoin miners rallied as direct beneficiaries of accelerating infrastructure spending and constrained compute capacity. Within crypto, renewed progress on the CLARITY Act supported exchanges and stablecoin-related companies, although the probability of the bill becoming law this year remains relatively low. Corporate blockchain adoption was otherwise limited during the week, with investor attention shifting towards a busy earnings calendar and the upcoming FOMC meeting. Week 30 key developments in Blockchain Equities: Index performance: The Index rose 6.9% during the week, outperforming Bitcoin, which was broadly unchanged. Oil prices moved sharply higher amid renewed concerns over Middle East supply, pushing the US 10-year Treasury yield towards 4.7% and reviving inflation concerns. The yield curve bear flattened as short-term yields rose more sharply than longer-term yields, supported by initial jobless claims falling to their lowest level since 1969. Markets are now pricing approximately two US interest-rate increases by year-end, while the ECB held rates unchanged but left the door open to further tightening as higher energy prices increase inflation risks. Block Index key movers: 7-day top performers : Cipher Digital (+45.7%), Hut-8 (+28.0%), RIOT Platforms (+26.8%) 7-day worst performers : Meta Platforms (-8.8%), Canaan (-7.6%), Block Inc (-6.2%) Bitcoin miners lead Index gains on accelerating AI infrastructure demand - Bitcoin miners and former miners were the largest positive contributors to the Index this week, as a series of announcements reinforced the value of their power and data-centre assets. Hut 8 signed a second 15-year, 352MW lease at its Beacon Point campus, increasing total contracted AI capacity to 949MW and aggregate base-term contract value to US$26.6bn. IREN announced US$2.8bn of new AI-cloud contracts and raised its year-end annualised revenue run-rate target to more than US$4bn, while Galaxy priced US$3.51bn of secured debt to fund the next phase of its contracted Helios campus. The announcements were supported by Alphabet raising its 2026 capital-expenditure guidance and stating that it expects to rely increasingly on third-party data-centre capacity while its own infrastructure is built. This suggests hyperscaler demand continues to exceed available capacity, benefiting miners that control large-scale power and development sites, and helping explain their strong contribution to the Index despite only a modest increase in Bitcoin prices. Earnings Recap – Key Holdings: CME Group, Nextera Energy – Positive Other news - index constituents: The CLARITY Act gained momentum after revised ethics provisions removed a key obstacle to Senate consideration, supporting Coinbase and Circle briefly during the week. Clearer market-structure rules would benefit Coinbase’s trading and custody businesses and encourage broader institutional use of Circle’s USDC. However, passage remains uncertain, with Polymarket assigning a 39% probability of approval by year-end. Coinbase launched USDC-settled perpetual futures linked to Circle, Robinhood and Strategy for eligible non-US users, offering 24/7 trading and leverage of up to 10 times. The launch extends Coinbase’s derivatives strategy beyond digital assets and creates a new way to trade crypto-equity exposure through a crypto exchange. Strategy increased its USD reserve by US$225m to approximately US$3.2bn, while its Bitcoin holdings remained unchanged at 843,775 BTC. The move reflects the company’s increased focus on maintaining liquidity to support preferred dividends and debt-interest payments. AMD announced a strategic partnership with Anthropic to deploy up to 2GW of AMD Instinct MI450 GPUs. Microsoft also agreed to deploy next-generation AMD Instinct accelerators and EPYC processors, while AMD and Cerebras announced a joint low-latency AI inference solution. The announcements materially expand AMD’s contracted AI-compute opportunity and support demand across the wider data-centre supply chain. Standard Chartered-backed Anchorpoint Financial is reportedly preparing to launch its regulated HKD-pegged stablecoin, HKDAP, during July. Listed exchanges OSL and HashKey are expected to distribute the token, creating potential revenue opportunities across trading, custody, conversion and payments. Other news – non - index constituents: Stablecoin-focused financial infrastructure company Augustus raised US$180m at a reported US$1bn valuation to develop a stablecoin-enabled clearing bank focused on cross-border and correspondent-banking services. BNY reportedly plans to pilot tokenised US Treasuries on its private blockchain by year-end, with the longer-term objective of supporting round-the-clock settlement for conventional and tokenised Treasuries by 2027. Jack Mallers stepped down as CEO of Twenty One Capital following the collapse of a proposed merger involving Twenty One, Strike and Elektron Energy. Twenty One reportedly holds 43,514 Bitcoin, making it one of the largest listed corporate Bitcoin holders, but the management change and failed transaction introduce additional uncertainty around its strategy and corporate structure. Shareholders of UK-listed Satsuma Technology reportedly approved the liquidation of the company’s remaining 668 Bitcoin treasury and the cancellation of its London listing. The company had raised approximately US$218m through convertible notes in 2025 but suffered a severe decline in its share price as Bitcoin weakened and financing obligations increased. The development highlights the refinancing, dilution and governance risks associated with leveraged digital-asset treasury strategies. Published on Jul 24th, 2026 Writer Satish Patel Investment Analyst Co-manages the Invesco CoinShares Global Blockchain ETF with expertise in payments and technology.

title: Safehold Closes Two Affordable Housing Ground Leases in California
summary: NEW YORK, July 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Safehold Inc. (NYSE: SAFE), the creator and leader of the modern ground lease industry, closed on two ground leases in June for the development of Affordable Housing communities in California, which will provide a total of 570 units upon completion.
body_text: Release Details Safehold Closes Two Affordable Housing Ground Leases in California July 14, 2026 PDF Version NEW YORK , July 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Safehold Inc. (NYSE: SAFE), the creator and leader of the modern ground lease industry, closed on two ground leases in June for the development of Affordable Housing communities in California, which will provide a total of 570 units upon completion. The Low-Income Housing Tax Credit developments are located in the Simi Valley area of Ventura County and the San Ysidro area of San Diego County. Both projects will be developed by The Pacific Companies, one of the most active Affordable Housing developers in the U.S. and a repeat Safehold customer. "We're thrilled to expand our relationship with The Pacific Companies, as we continue to grow Safehold's focus on the Affordable Housing sector," said Steve Wylder, Safehold's Head of Investments. "We've now closed more than 25 ground leases on LIHTC developments throughout the State of California, where there's significant unmet demand for high-quality Affordable product." The developments are supported by tax credit equity from U.S. Bank and Wells Fargo, respectively. "We're positioning our capital as a tool to fill capital structure gaps and move projects forward, and we're excited to see the growing adoption of the ground lease structure amongst developers and their debt and equity sources," Wylder added. Additional information on Safehold's Affordable Housing platform is available at www.safeholdaffordablehousing.com . About Safehold: Safehold Inc. (NYSE: SAFE) is revolutionizing real estate ownership by providing a new and better way for owners to unlock the value of the land beneath their buildings. Having created the modern ground lease industry in 2017, Safehold continues to help owners of high quality multifamily, affordable housing, office, industrial, hospitality, student housing, life science and mixed-use properties generate higher returns with less risk. The Company, which is taxed as a real estate investment trust (REIT), seeks to deliver safe, growing income and long-term capital appreciation to its shareholders. title: Digi International Adds Open-Standard SMARC® Form Factor to the Digi ConnectCore 95 Family, Now Shipping Globally
summary: Designed to simplify the move to open standards, the Digi ConnectCore 95 SMARC module, built on the NXP i.MX 95 processor, delivers performance, connectivity and scale, with security and lifecycle management services included.
